content.title: About
content.content: Fry sauce is a popular American condiment that blends the flavors of tomato ketchup and mayonnaise. It is commonly served with french fries, chicken nuggets, and other fried foods. The sauce has a creamy texture with a mildly sweet and slightly tangy taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fry sauce originated in the United States in the 1950s and quickly became a fast‑food favorite.
The classic recipe includes tomato paste, mayonnaise, vinegar, sugar, and spices such as paprika and garlic.
In different regions the sauce has various names: in Utah it is called “fry sauce,” while in parts of the Midwest it is known as “red mayo.”
Home cooks often experiment with fry sauce as a chicken marinade or a base for barbecue sauces.
Its popularity surged in the 2020s thanks to social media where users share homemade versions.

items.title: Source of Vitamin A
items.content: Tomato ingredients provide beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A, supporting vision.

items.title: Contains Vitamin E
items.content: The mayonnaise component supplies vitamin E, an antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Provides Healthy Fats
items.content: Mayonnaise contains monounsaturated fats that can be heart‑friendly when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Rich in Lycopene
items.content: Tomatoes are high in lycopene, a compound linked to reduced risk of certain chronic diseases.

items.title: Enhances Satiety
items.content: The balance of sweet, sour, and salty flavors can make meals more satisfying, potentially helping control overall calorie intake.

items.title: High Calorie Content
items.content: The combination of mayonnaise and sugar makes the sauce calorie‑dense; large portions may contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Sugar and Salt Levels
items.content: Excessive sugar and salt can affect blood glucose and blood pressure.

items.title: Egg Allergy
items.content: Mayonnaise is typically made with egg yolks, making the sauce unsuitable for people with egg allergies.

items.title: Preservatives in Commercial Versions
items.content: Some store‑bought sauces contain artificial preservatives and stabilizers that may cause sensitivity in certain individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve fry sauce with french fries, chicken nuggets, fish sticks, burgers, or as a dip for vegetable sticks. It can also be spread on sandwiches, added to salads, or used as a base for more complex sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the sauce refrigerated in a sealed container. After opening, use within 1‑2 weeks. Discard if the smell, color, or taste changes.
